title: Verify the AI Summary
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Judge whether each of six statements in an AI-written summary is supported by a short source passage.

educational.topic: Checking AI output against a source
learningObjectives: The learner will judge whether each of six statements in an AI-written summary is supported by a source passage, correctly judging at least five of six on the first attempt.
prerequisites: AI hallucination, grounding in a source, and AI literacy, from the section "AI Hallucination and AI Literacy" in Chapter 5.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Judge each claim against a source, with the matching sentence highlighted as feedback
keyQuestions: Which sentence of the passage says this?
Is the statement changed, invented, or exact?
commonMisconceptions: A confident, fluent statement is probably correct
A statement that sounds plausible is supported
A summary that is mostly right can be trusted whole
assessmentOpportunities: The summary says the pilot lasted a full semester. Supported?
The summary says students were assigned at random. Supported?
The summary says a university team ran the evaluation, and the passage does not say who did. Supported?
Five of six statements check out. Can you trust the summary whole?

controls.name: Supported, Not supported
controls.description: choose your judgment for the statement.

controls.name: Submit
controls.description: commits it. Two attempts per statement; only the first counts.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: moves to the next statement; after the sixth it shows your score.

controls.name: Show the rule
controls.description: checkbox that shows how to judge a statement.
